expected.title: The key formula identifying a difference of divisors weighted by orders with the divisor of the tame symbol
expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: The key formula equates two cycles on X: one built from orders of the local sections f_i and g_i multiplied by the divisors of the trivialising sections of two invertible sheaves, the other from the divisors of the tame symbols partial_{B_i}(f_i, g_i) (statement lines 4745-4758, tag 0AYC). The proof establishes invariance of the identity under rescaling the local trivialising sections, which mixes well-definedness of divisors with the bilinearity and normalisation property of the tame symbol, and then reduces to comparing a single coefficient by localising at a two-dimensional Noetherian local domain and choosing trivialisations so that the first expression collapses. The reduction is the substance of the argument, so the claim is H2.

expected.title: An object of the derived category is invertible exactly when it is locally a shift of the ring, and then its cohomology is finite projective in a single degree per factor
expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R and an object M of D(R) and gives two equivalent conditions: that M be invertible with respect to the tensor product in D(R); and that for every prime p there exist f not in p and an integer n with M_f isomorphic to R_f[-n]. It then asserts four consequences in the invertible case: that M is perfect; that M is the direct sum of its shifted cohomology objects; that each H^n(M) is a finite projective module; and that R decomposes as a product over a range of degrees on which the corresponding cohomology module is invertible (source lines 38656-38675). The proof is a real local-to-global argument. For (2) implies (1) it forms R Hom_R(M, R) and the composition map R Hom(M, R) tensor^L_R M -> R, sees by local checking that this is an isomorphism in a step stated to be omitted, and concludes that M is invertible because D(R) is symmetric monoidal (proof lines 38678-38683). For (1) implies (2) it observes that an invertible object of a monoidal category has a left dual, namely its inverse, so M is perfect by the duals-and-perfection lemma; then for a prime p with residue field kappa it uses that M tensor^L_R kappa is an invertible object of D(kappa), which forces dim H^i(M tensor^L_R kappa) to be nonzero for exactly one i and equal to 1 there, and the lift-perfect-from-residue-field lemma then produces the required n (proof lines 38686-38695). The last part is the global assembly: the proof defines U_n as the union of the opens D(f) with M_f isomorphic to R_f[-n], notes U_n and U_{n'} are disjoint for n not equal to n', and if M has tor amplitude in [a, b] then U_n is empty for n outside that range; hence there is a product decomposition R = prod_{a <= n <= b} R_n with U_n corresponding to Spec(R_n), and since D(R) decomposes as the product of the D(R_n) the remaining assertions (b), (c) and (d) follow (proof lines 38698-38707). The non-routine content is the residue-field argument that forces the single-degree shape, and the product decomposition that promotes it to a global statement.

expected.difficulty_reason: The author constructs a countable quasi-isomorphic differential graded subalgebra by repeatedly killing all countable kernel classes, then a countable semi-free resolution and a sequential exhaustion by finite differential-closed cell submodules. The coupled algebra/model reduction and finite-cell closure construction give a substantive derived finiteness characterization beyond qualification homological algebra.

expected.title: Simultaneous étale approximation of relative completed local maps over a locally Noetherian G-ring base
expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: Both the base map and the relative map must be approximated while preserving their compatibility to a prescribed adic order. The proof combines local-map approximation with Popescu smoothing and finite-presentation descent to transport an étale model through a smooth intermediate algebra before specializing it back to an elementary étale neighbourhood.

expected.title: Noetherian approximation of a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme extending a prescribed affine-transition finite-type integer model system on a quasi-compact open
expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: The theorem extends a prescribed finite-type integer model of a quasi-compact open across an arbitrary qcqs scheme. Its proof builds fibre-product rings, recovers standard affine opens after finite-stage descent, manufactures finite-type subalgebra models, and synchronizes two-level directed gluing with affine transitions. This global relative Noetherian approximation construction is substantially beyond ordinary affine finite-presentation descent.

expected.title: A sufficient condition for compatibility of the cycle class map with pushforward
expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the compatibility of the cycle class map with pushforward follows from the special case of a closed immersion whose conormal class in K theory is a pullback class (statement lines 5257-5264). The proof (proof lines 5265-5300) reduces to a closed immersion, introduces a Grassmannian bundle to make the conormal class a pullback, and verifies the hypothesis through the conormal sequence. H3: a multi step reduction, written out in full.

expected.title: Uniform Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity bounds for kernels of fixed-rank trivial-sheaf quotients with fixed Hilbert polynomial
expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: Hyperplane induction controls higher cohomology but leaves the first cohomology obstruction unbounded. The proof shows that any nondecreasing step forces all subsequent steps to be injective and hence zero by eventual vanishing, so strict dimension drops and the Hilbert polynomial give a uniform bound.
